MICROSOFT OUTAGE

The string of service outages began on Thursday, 12 November 2026, at Microsoft when a global outage disrupted Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook email, Teams, AI assistant Copilot and other workplace tools, throwing everyday business services into disarray worldwide. Businesses, airlines, and government agencies in more than 70 countries were affected. Internet search tools making use of Microsoft's services, such as Microsoft Bing, DuckDuckGo and ChatGPT, were also affected worldwide. The outage lasted till the morning of November 14, 2026, in the USA.

Microsoft said that the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or AI agents. It blamed the outage to a bug that came in with a July update to its networking gateway servers on settings applied to servers after an update.

FAA’S NATIONWIDE FLIGHT GROUNDING

ABC News reported that The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a rare nationwide ground stop for all airports Friday, 13 November 2026, a more than four-hour disruption that snarled travel from coast to coast with more than 14,000 flights canceled on Friday and Saturday.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said at a press conference, “The ground stop on Friday was the result of faulty equipment. We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related."

Scott Kirby, the CEO of United Airlines called Friday's nationwide ground stop a "call to action" stating that "our Air Traffic Control system needs more investment in modern technology to ensure better redundancy and reliability now."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explained in a press conference on Friday that what we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system. He asked that Americans call their members of Congress to demand that the FAA be given another $50 billion on top of the $12.5 billion it already received in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, most of which remains unspent, according to members of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

A faulty router was blamed for the nationwide ground stop. But a spokesperson for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which owns Juniper, the company that manufactured the routers believed to be central to the ground stop, said in a statement to ABC News that the devices were working properly Friday, when the ground stop occurred.

FAA administrator Bryan Bedford’s statement, “We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related” requires some scrutiny. Perhaps Mr. Bedford meant that no cyberattack was involved which is likely true. But why did he need to state there is “zero evidence of anything AI-related.”

The system rolled out across the country on Tuesday, November 10, and caused public concern after the nationwide grounding of air traffic on Friday, November 13, 2026. Alfonso is Sean Duffy’s son-in-law and at 26 is the youngest member of the U.S. Congress.

Probably that’s why Duffy and Bedford had to strongly deny that the AI system was related in any way to the data glitch that led to the nationwide ground stop.

OTHER OUTAGES

Also on Monday, tens of thousands of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Truist Bank customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts and the money transfer service Zelle experienced outage. Chase said that a technical issue at the bank caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. The bank also stated that the technical problems were not the result of a cyberattack,

Apple services such as Apple Pay, Apple Music, App Store and AppleCare Services suffered full outages on Tuesday, 17 November and some users were prevented from signing in to iCloud. The company stated that an internal update caused these outages.

Marriott International, the largest U.S. hotel operator, also experienced technology issues that guests reported had impacted reservations and check-ins.

EXPLANATIONS BY THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

President Trump and other administration officials have offered their explanations for this string of almost simultaneous massive outages.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a “nefarious attack” on the FAA. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s explanation was that “Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data,” after a newly installed router fired roughly 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds.”

Traveling with the President, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that “We are not under systemic attack,” and that there was “zero evidence whatsoever” the disruptions were connected and that “Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause.” According to Forbes, he further explained that when companies patch vulnerabilities, it can create a “short-term disruption in the way your system works.”

A top intelligence official said that recent tech outages are not due to state sponsored attack.

President Trump told reporters: “It’s like when you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine.”

Opinion of many experts is that one or two incidents can be a coincidence. But so many within five days indicate a pattern.

One expert said that the explanation that outages were caused by upgrades is strange because system upgrades are not done at 12.00 or 1.00 p.m. but at night.

Speaking with reporters regarding the outages, Senator Josh Hawley (R-MO) expressed the public’s and the experts’ skepticism best when he said that if the outages were coincidental, it would be "like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world," adding, "You can't tell me that all of this just is happenstance.
